name: Music Practice and Composition
title: Music Practice and Composition
answer: AI can support music practice and composition by providing accompaniment tracks, generating theory drills, and offering feedback on student work, but it must not replace the student's own creative choices or the teacher's role as the primary source of feedback. The idea matters because it makes lonely home practice more like rehearsal and gives students more chances to repeat what they find hard, while keeping authorship firmly with the student.

crumbs.name: Arts, Music, Physical Education, and Health

sections.body: This idea is about using AI to support two parts of music learning: practice and composition. Practice is where musicians improve, but it is often lonely, so practice tracks that play the other parts or provide accompaniment make home practice feel more like rehearsal. Teachers can record their own tracks, and some software can adjust tempo or key. For composition, a student might ask an approved tool for feedback on a melody, such as whether phrases feel balanced or the ending resolves. The problem it solves is giving students more support and repetition without taking over the creative work that belongs to them.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In the classroom, teachers can use AI to generate music theory drills on intervals, key signatures, or chord progressions and deliver them through Google Forms for quick feedback, letting students practice at their own pace and repeat what they find hard. For practice at home, teachers can record their own practice tracks, and some music software can adjust tempo or key to match a student's level. For composition, a student composer might ask an approved tool for feedback on a melody, such as whether the phrases feel balanced or the ending resolves. The text does not give separate grade bands for these practices. Across all of them, the teacher checks the drills for accuracy, since AI tools can mislabel notes or chords, and the teacher remains the main source of feedback.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The book labels this idea with a study: a study of 343 students in music schools in Beijing found that intelligent practice tools helped students improve on their instruments, though gains varied by instrument and the study did not use random assignment (Li et al., 2023). No other evidence is given for the composition or theory drill parts of the idea.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: Composition feedback needs more care. The feedback can spark ideas, but it should never rewrite the student's music, the teacher remains the main source of feedback, and the student makes every creative choice. Music teachers should also be alert to AI composition tools that can generate complete songs from a short description. These can be interesting to study and discuss, but they fall squarely under the authorship rule when it comes to assignments. A student who submits a generated song as original composition has not learned to compose.
